EN: Radial-In / Radial-Out are the directions at 90 degrees to the current path of travel, pointing in and out. \nBurning these directions "rolls" the orbit as you can see below.
Burning in towards the planet will\n  lower the orbit ahead of your vessel.
Burning out along the plane will raise\nyour orbit ahead of your vessel.
Burning retrograde will decrease your\norbital velocity and lower the altitude\non the opposite side to your burn.
Burning prograde will increase your\norbital velocity and raise the altitude\non the opposite side to your burn.
You thrust in the prograde and retrograde directions to adjust the eccentricity of an orbit.

Dres is a very small planet. It was the first planet considered to be a dwarf. 
Its orbit is highly irregular and, together with its size, it took a long time to 
discover since half the time it was not where scientists expected to find a 
planet.
Some astronomers have noticed variations in gravitational measurements \naround Dres. While only slight, perhaps there is something more to this \ngray dwarf.
Due to its nature of frequenting the bad parts of space, this dwarf planet \nwas officially labeled as "Not to be trusted" by the scientific community.
Also known as the red dot that you can see if you squint at it really hard, \nDuna has long been a wonder to all kerbals.
The planet has been held in much awe due to its striking red color and \nstark contrast to the color green.
Ike is Duna's only moon, with steep \nrocky slopes; it's a challenging crash... \nI mean landing.

There’s been a considerable amount of controversy around the status of 
Eeloo as being a proper planet or just a "lump of ice going around the 
sun." 

The debate is still ongoing, as most academic summits held to address the 
issue have devolved into, on good days, petty name calling, and on worse 
ones, all-out brawls.
The furthest planet from the sun, Eeloo is like a riddle, wrapped in a \nmystery, inside an enigma, covered in ice.

It is considered by some to be an almost sister planet to Kerbin. Well, 
despite the purple, and the toxic atmosphere, and the extreme pressures 
and temperatures. Actually, it’s not very similar at all, is it? Who are those 
people?

Gilly is a lumpy rock wandering around the 
orbit of Eve. It is by far the smallest natural 
satellite that the Kerbal Astronomical 
Society has discovered.
Eve is certainly the purplest object in the solar system. It's one of the larger, \nmost visible objects, mainly because of its very, very purple tint.

Jool is particularly known for being a rather large, predominantly green planet. 
Kerbalkind has longed to visit it since it was first spotted in the sky. 

Philosophers reason that the swirling green planet must be a really nice place 
to visit, on account of its wholesome coloration.
Jool has five moons orbiting it: Laythe, Vall, Tylo, Bop and Pol.
If you look at Jool through a telescope, it is fuzzy.
